newsitem.title: USA: Rexworks says lower sales hurt Q2.
newsitem.headline: Rexworks says lower sales hurt Q2.

text.p: Rexworks Inc said Friday demand softened during the second quarter, causing a drop in sales compared to last year and hurting profits.

Earlier Rexworks posted a loss of $319 million, or $0.16 a share, in the second quarter compared to a profit of $131 million, or $0.07, in the same period last year. Sales fell to $11.4 million from $14.3 million.
"We experienced a softening of demand for our products during the second quarter," said Laurance Newman, president and chief executive of Rexworks.
"We also had a number of orders which could not be shipped and billed in the quarter. As a result, sales for the quarter were 21 percent lower than in the same period one year ago."

Selling, general and administrative expenses were lower in 1997 than in 1996, the company said. But reduction in expenses were not sufficient to offset the impact of lower gross profit on reduced sales and the impact of unfavorable manufacturing variances due to lower levels of production.
"Significant restructuring steps were taken at the end of the second quarter to lower our break-even point to match our current levels of sales activity," Newman said in a statement.
